summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with asymptomatic hypotension (70/50) noted at dialysis and increased right hip and knee pain. He has a history of ESRD, recent MRSA line infection on vancomycin, non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, and prior CVA with residual right leg weakness. Initial workup revealed hyperkalemia, treated emergently, and a new left femoral central line was placed for dialysis access. Imaging showed avascular necrosis of the right femoral head with joint degeneration and an old acetabular fracture. Knee aspiration was performed after initial refusal, with no growth on culture, ruling out septic arthritis. Blood cultures remained negative. He was managed conservatively with continuation of vancomycin for the prior MRSA infection, adjustment of dialysis fluid removal, and initiation of midodrine to support blood pressure during dialysis. Orthopedics recommended outpatient follow-up for possible hip replacement. The patient was discharged home with services, stable and afebrile, with clear instructions on medication, weight monitoring, and follow-up.
problems: Aseptic necrosis of head and neck of femur
Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
Osteoarthrosis, unspecified whether generalized or localized, lower leg
